notes: Spec + schema amended in lockstep per schema-first rule; mirror is byte-identical (regenerated via npm run generate -w @openpacker/contracts, which writes packages/contracts/schemas itself). New $defs.DelegatedAdapterBin (name safe-segment pattern, relative POSIX path pattern refusing absolute + '..', interpreter enum node|python|dotnet|native, entry maxLength 1024 — 'entry required iff python' is normative prose in the spec and must be enforced host-side in layer 02; JSON Schema cannot express that per-bin conditional cleanly here). DelegatedAdapterInspectionResult.executables is optional, maxItems 64. generated.ts now exports type DelegatedAdapterBin and ProviderInspection-side consumers will see executables on the wire type. The host-fetch marker openpacker/artifact-bytes: "host-fetch" is specified as a provider capability extension (adapter-core ProviderCapabilities.extensions is a free-form record, cf. existing 'openpacker.dev/ecosystem' key) — layer 02 must surface it from the plugin host; it does NOT fit common.schema.json Extensions propertyNames (no slashes), so it was deliberately not put in the RegistryDefinition extensions container. Conformance gained 4 negative vectors (dotdot path, absolute path, unsafe name, unknown interpreter). docs/plans/plugin-execution/sdlc-state.md remains untracked; coordinator owns it. No runtime .ts behavior changed beyond regenerated contracts.
deviations: Task said to add the executables example to fixtures/protocol/delegated-adapter/example.json, but that file is a DelegatedAdapterManifest (additionalProperties: false — executables would fail validation). The inspect example validated against DelegatedAdapterInspectionResult is inspection-result.json, so the executables array (one node-interpreter bin) was added there instead.
